title: BI 764198 (TRPC6i) – Study 1434-0027/1434-0019: Phase II Basket Trial in Proteinuric Glomerular Diseases / DMD Development Plan

background.text: Study 1434-0027 is a potential Phase 2 multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled basket trial evaluating BI 764198 in proteinuric glomerular diseases with podocyte involvement. Key inclusion criteria include eGFR ≥25, optimized SoC, and biopsy-proven disease.
background.quote: Potential phase 2, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled basket trial to evaluate BI 764198 in proteinuric glomerular diseases with podocyte involvement

background.text: Global study 1434-0019 Ph II timeline: pre-IND submission planned 19 Dec 2025, feedback by 30 Jan 2026 (30 WD Type I HAI); CTA submission/approval 17 May–14 Aug 2026; FSS–LSS 16 Jun 2026–26 Jul 2027; key results 4 May 2028. China study 1434-0019 Ph II: fSIV–LSS 17 Nov 2026–26 Jul 2027.
background.quote: Pre-IND under preparation with planned submission on 19 Dec. The review will follow the Type I HAI for 30 WD.

title: BI 3034701 (GGY2Ra.) – Study 1507-0002: Obesity Phase II Development Plan

background.text: PoC was achieved in Phase I; Ph I results not yet released. Phase II design is under re-discussion for acceleration (Ph II/III seamless, shortened maintenance dose period, reduced dose groups). Recruitment window is only 2 months (could be longer if new CTA process implemented).

title: BI 3802876 (FAP/TRAILR2 bispecific antibody) – MASH Cirrhosis: Asian Phase 1 and China Integration Plan

background.text: Phase I in healthy volunteers showed a slight increase in hs-cTNT indicating cardiovascular concerns. Global Phase 2a (US and Canada only) to be initiated Dec 2025 to demonstrate anti-fibrosis effect and assess benefit-risk in MASH cirrhosis. China approval base case: Aug 2037.
background.quote:
A slight increase in hs-cTNT indicating cardiovascular concerns was observed in Phase I among healthy volunteers.
A Phase 2a trial (US and Canada only) will be initiated to demonstrate the anti-fibrosis effect and to assess the benefit-risk profile in MASH cirrhosis patients.
